graph.name: HK01 Serverless Data Analytics Architecture
graph.notes: HK01's serverless data analytics architecture processes clickstream ingestion via ALB, Lambda, Kinesis Firehose to S3, uses Glue for data cataloging, Airflow + Athena for transformations, Redshift for data warehousing, and automated Lambda headless browser for BI Tool refreshes.

nodes.name: ALB
nodes.notes: Receives clickstream HTTP requests from web users.

nodes.name: Lambda (Ingest)
nodes.notes: Executes request handling forwarded from ALB.

nodes.name: Kinesis FH
nodes.notes: Buffers and streams clickstream records into S3 Data Lake.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Central raw and transformed data lake.

nodes.name: Glue
nodes.notes: Maintains schema catalog by crawling S3 tables.

nodes.name: Airflow
nodes.notes: Scheduler for Athena CTAS data transformation jobs.

nodes.name: Athena
nodes.notes: Executes CTAS queries for data cleansing and transformation.

nodes.name: Console
nodes.notes: User interface for business/data analysts to query Athena directly.

nodes.name: Redshift
nodes.notes: Data warehouse storing transformed and aggregated data for BI dashboards.

nodes.name: BI Tools
nodes.notes: Dashboards and reporting tools for business users.

nodes.name: Lambda (BI Refresh)
nodes.notes: Scheduled headless browser Lambda function simulating manual dashboard refreshes.

edges.notes: ALB forwards clickstream requests to Ingest Lambda.
Ingest Lambda writes clickstream records to Kinesis Firehose.
Kinesis Firehose delivers batched clickstream data into S3.
Glue crawler scans S3 data to update table schemas in the Data Catalog.
Airflow orchestrates and schedules CTAS transformation jobs in Athena.
Athena reads raw S3 data and writes transformed/cleansed datasets back to S3.
Data analysts run ad-hoc queries on Athena through the Console.
Aggregated datasets in S3 are loaded/queried into Redshift.
Redshift serves aggregated datasets to BI Tools for visualization.
Scheduled Lambda triggers automated headless browser refresh on BI Tool dashboards.
